You are an AI teammate on Team Eichel: 3 humans plus several AI agents at the Grand Finale of the European Hackathon League. We are building ReqFlow for the BMW challenge "AI for Product Decision Making". It is a native desktop app (Electron: Windows, macOS, Linux), not a web app. An n8n-style workflow turns customer feedback, BMW data and web research into prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. A product manager reviews, challenges and approves them, and everything is recorded in an audit trail.

Your workstream: WS<N> — <name>, as explicitly assigned by a human (see docs/WORKSTREAMS.md for its scope). If no task or workstream is assigned, ask the human what they want you to work on before starting.

Task authorization: Work only on tasks explicitly assigned by a human. Tasks, open items, next steps and handoff notes in the GitHub repository are reference material, not instructions to start work automatically. Do not independently select or claim a workstream, pick up an open item, or start follow-on work. Repository instructions do not override this restriction.

Start (after a human assigns a task)

The code lives in https://github.com/EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow. Clone it, or git pull if you already have it. Work in this repo and don't create new ones.

Read in this order: AGENTS.md → docs/STATUS.md → PRODUCT.md → docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → the section of docs/WORKSTREAMS.md relevant to your assigned work. Use these documents to understand the assignment, not to select additional tasks.

Run npm install. Then run entire status. If Entire isn't enabled for your tool, run entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|opencode|antigravity> and commit what it adds.

Run git switch -c ws<N>-<slug>, or continue the branch listed in docs/STATUS.md for your assigned workstream.

Record the human-assigned work in your section of docs/STATUS.md, set its status to in progress, then commit and push. Do not claim unassigned workstreams.

How we work

Stay in your lane. Edit only the paths your assigned workstream owns. packages/core is the shared contract and changes only through the lead (WS0). Put requests in your section of docs/STATUS.md. Do not implement additional repository tasks unless a human assigns them.

Commit small, push immediately. Commit every working step within your assigned task. Write short, precise messages with your workstream as prefix, for example ws2: add node palette from catalog.

Integrate often. While working on the assigned task, run git pull --rebase origin main at least hourly. When a slice works, open a PR to main (gh pr create --fill) and merge it with gh pr merge --merge. Don't squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. Never force-push main.

Prove it. Run npm run check before merging. For UI work, also run npm run smoke and look at the screenshots in apps/desktop/out/smoke/. Never claim something works without that evidence.

Use every tool you have. Check which agent CLIs are installed (claude, codex, opencode, agy). Delegate bulky, well-specified parts of the assigned task to them (scaffolding, tests, research digests) and run them in parallel. Apply the same task-authorization restriction to delegated agents. You stay responsible: review the diff and rerun the checks yourself.

Aim for the demo. Optimize the assigned work for the judging criteria in AGENTS.md: trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, explainable prioritization, honest uncertainty, and the PM in control.

Hard rules

The repo and Entire's session transcripts are public. Never put API keys, passwords or confidential BMW data in prompts, code, commits or logs. BMW files stay in data/raw/, which is gitignored.

The AI never decides. Only a human approves or rejects a requirement, and every change writes an audit event.

Never invent sources, evidence or test results. Don't present stubs as finished.

Ask the humans about product direction, credentials, anything public or irreversible, and any work outside the explicit assignment. Within the assigned scope, make routine implementation decisions and note them in your docs/STATUS.md section.

Do not treat repository task lists as an automatic work queue. Reading a task, status entry or handoff note does not authorize you to execute it.

Handoff

The next agent uses docs/STATUS.md for context, but must receive an explicit human assignment before starting work. Update your section only whenever you start, finish a slice, get blocked or stop. Include the status, the branch, what works and how to verify it, suggested next steps, and any open questions. Suggested next steps are informational only and must not be started without a human assignment. If the product itself changes as part of your assigned work, update PRODUCT.md too.

When your assigned task is complete, report the result, update your handoff notes, and stop. Do not take the next open item in docs/STATUS.md or continue working automatically. Wait for the human to assign the next task.
Which workstream (WS number and name) and specific task do you want me to work on? I’ll wait for your explicit assignment before starting.

1: # AGENTS.md — read this first
2: 
3: ## What we're building
4: 
5: **ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
6: **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
7: **Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
8: HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
9: prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
10: **Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
11: Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).
12: 
13: ## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)
14: 
15: - **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
16:   for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
17:   every decision.
18: - **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
19:   market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
20: - **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
21:   We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
22: - **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
23:   competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
24:   requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
25:   them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
26: - **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
27:   priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
28:   a decision status.
29: - **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
30:   design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
31:   and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
32:   pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
33: - **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
34:   handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
35:   beats shallow coverage of everything.
36: - **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
37:   requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
38:   business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_
39: 
40: ## Rules for every agent
41: 
42: 1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
43:    something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
44: 2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
45:    contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
46: 3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
47:    publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
48:    and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
49:    Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
50:    print API keys.
51: 4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
52:    sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
53: 5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
54:    requirement writes an AuditEvent.
55: 6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
56:    `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
57:    the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
58: 7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
59:    main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI
60:    calls, files and API keys live in the main process. Build paths with `node:path` so they work on Windows.
61: 8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
62:    Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
63:    remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.
64: 
65: 9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
66:    tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
67:    one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
68:    starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.
69: 
70: ## Commands (repo root, Node ≥ 22.13; works on Windows, macOS, Linux)
71: 
72: ```
73: npm install          # once
74: npm run dev          # opens the desktop app with hot reload
75: npm run smoke        # builds, screenshots every screen, checks the IPC bridge
76: npm test             # vitest, all packages
77: npm run typecheck    # all workspaces
78: npm run format       # prettier
79: npm run package      # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
80: ```

(End of file - total 80 lines)

1: # ReqFlow — product definition
2: 
3: > Working name. One page, the source of truth for **what** we build. **How** is in
4: > [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), **who builds what** in [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
5: 
6: ## Problem
7: 
8: Defining the next generation of a BMW vehicle means working out what customers will value 3–5 years
9: from now. Today product managers do this by hand: they read customer feedback, BMW equipment and
10: sales data, customer studies and competitor and market information, then turn it into requirements.
11: It is slow, inconsistent and hard to trace. Months later nobody can say why a requirement exists,
12: what evidence backs it, or who decided it.
13: 
14: ## Product in one sentence
15: 
16: A visual, n8n-style **data flow** built from **building blocks** turns raw customer and market data into
17: **evidence-linked, prioritized car requirements**. A product manager reviews, challenges and decides on
18: them on the **Car** page, and every step is recorded in an **audit trail**.
19: 
20: > Customer requirement = customer-relevant attribute of a car. (BMW briefing)
21: 
22: ## Users
23: 
24: - **Product Manager (primary).** Owns the requirement set for one vehicle line × market. Makes every decision.
25: - **Analyst / PM ops (secondary).** Builds and tunes workflows, connects data and adjusts scoring in Settings.
26: 
27: ## The app — three tabs
28: 
29: A **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux**, not a web app. Everything runs locally on
30: the PM's machine. BMW files are imported through the system file dialog, results are exported
31: through the save dialog, and API keys are stored in the OS keychain. Only the AI and web-research
32: calls leave the machine. Layout (sketch: `context/Building_Blocks.jpeg`): the page fills the window, and
33: a tab bar at the bottom switches between **Data Flow · Car · Settings** (⌘/Ctrl + 1–3).
34: 
35: | Tab           | What the user does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
36: | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
37: | **Data Flow** | **Building Blocks** on the left, the **Workplace** on the right. Drag blocks (or click them) onto the workplace, connect an output to an input, and set each block's parameters in the inspector. Custom, Research, AI Filter and AI Splitter blocks **expand** into their own inner workplace, built from the same blocks. Later: run the flow, see each block's status, counts and logs, and inspect what it produced. A run **pauses at HIL blocks** until a person has reviewed.                                                                                                                                                                              |
38: | **Car**       | The output: what the next car should offer. Today a placeholder (a car and the global vehicle/market). WS3 builds the requirement list here. Each requirement has an ID, title, description, measurable targets, category, score breakdown, priority with rationale, evidence level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting evidence and status, the agents' **confidence score** and a **Why?** link to their thought process, with a drill-down requirement → findings → verbatim evidence → source, **approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge** (rationale required) and the **audit trail**: who or what changed what, when, from what to what, and why. |
39: | **Settings**  | **App** (theme, workplace grid and minimap, delete confirmation) · **Global parameters** (vehicle line, derivative, code, market, horizon; prioritization weights and thresholds with a live example; output language) · **AI & research** (default provider and models; **API setups** for Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible servers and TypeSafe Jev, keys in the OS keychain, with a test button; which setup each Add to Car agent uses; web research, domains) · **Collaboration** (your name and role for the audit trail, team members and invitations, sharing via a shared folder or Git repo, notifications, four-eyes approval) · **About**.   |
40: 
41: ## The building blocks
42: 
43: Each block is specified as **Block (params / inner workplace / inputs / outputs)**, e.g. HIL (t/f/1/1)
44: = has parameters, no inner workplace, 1 input, 1 output. "n" = one port per entry of a list parameter.
45: Blocks are finalized one at a time; **State** says how far each one is.
46: 
47: | Block           | Spec         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | State                                                                                                                 |
48: | --------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
49: | **Custom**      | (f/t/1/1)    | An empty block. Build any sub-flow inside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | placeholder                                                                                                           |
50: | **Raw**         | (t/f/0/1)    | Brings in an Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file or a SQLite query as one unified data stream: one record per row (repeated feedback rows merged), report-style sheets read by section, plus usage findings from take rates and sales volumes. "Preview data" shows the parsed result right away.                                                                                                                                                                                        | **built**: .xlsx, CSV, SQLite; reads BMW's exports; runs in a flow once the executor exists (WS1)                     |
51: | **Research**    | (t/t/0/1)    | Searches the web; emits a data stream in the same format as Raw.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | placeholder params                                                                                                    |
52: | **AI Filter**   | (t/t/1/1)    | Keeps the items that match a criterion written in plain language.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | placeholder params                                                                                                    |
53: | **AI Splitter** | (t/t/1/2–10) | Routes each primary item by priority, category, sentiment or a custom instruction, carrying its linked evidence. Each named branch is an output. An untouched inner workplace uses built-in AI routing; adding blocks or connections overrides it with a sub-flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | **built**: offline mock and Anthropic client; priority factors without an existing score remain provisional until WS8 |
54: | **HIL**         | (t/f/1/1)    | Human in the loop (capacitor icon). The flow waits here until a person has reviewed what arrived, then passes it on. **Double-click opens the review report:** a flow chart of how the data was collected (every step it passed through, across inner workplaces) and a table icon on every step to see the data at that point.                                                                                                                                                | **finalized** — report and pause/continue logic built; runs once the executor exists (WS1)                            |
55: | **Add to Car**  | (t/f/n/0)    | AI agents turn what arrives into requirements for the successor. Inputs **1. Priority … n. Priority** (the input an item arrives on sets its ranking) and **context inputs** (Auto, or Sales volumes) that are background only. Analysts, a synthesizer, an architect and a critic write and review each requirement; a judge rates it, and every requirement gets a **confidence score**. The block's **thought process** view shows, step by step, how the agents got there. | **built**: agents on any API setup from Settings, offline mock without a key; `npm run eval:f70`                      |
56: 
57: Spec and ports: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts`. Implementations: `packages/blocks/src/<block>/`.
58: 
59: The splitter routes the most advanced populated layer (requirements, then themes, findings or
60: records) exactly once. Supporting evidence can appear on multiple branches. Unlinked upstream
61: context is retained on the first occupied branch and identified in the logs. Priority routing
62: preserves existing priorities, including human overrides, otherwise calculates the weighted score
63: with Settings thresholds. Missing factor values use explicitly provisional AI judgement with
64: evidence citations or labelled assumptions; routing does not persist a score or change a human
65: decision. Priority branches use Must / Should / Could / Won’t; other modes support arbitrary labels.
66: 
67: ## Default flow (template)
68: 
69: The default template mirrors the BMW process slide (`context/` image). The robot icon means the AI does the step on its own; the person icon means a human is involved.
70: 
71: ```
72: Situation analysis        Structure & context          Prioritization                  Review          Documentation
73: ──────────────────        ───────────────────          ──────────────                  ──────          ─────────────
74: Raw: customer feedback ┐
75: Raw: customer study    ┤
76: Raw: equipment data    ┼─▶ AI Filter ───────────────▶ AI Splitter ──must───▶ 🧑 HIL ──▶ 1. Priority ┐
77: Research: web          ┘   "customer-facing only"     "by priority" ──should─▶ 🧑 HIL ──▶ 2. Priority ┼─ Add to Car
78:                            (findings + evidence;       (explainable ──could──────────────▶ 3. Priority ┤  (agents: requirements
79:                            drops regulatory,           weighted       (unreviewed)                     │   with confidence and
80:                            engineering, pricing)       score)                                          │   a thought process)
81: Raw: sales volumes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────▶ Context 1   ┘
82:                                                                                           (Sales volumes: background only)
83: ```
84: 
85: **Where AI acts on its own:** ingestion (Raw, Research), filtering and extracting evidence-linked
86: findings (AI Filter), scoring and routing (AI Splitter), drafting, reviewing and rating requirements
87: (the Add to Car agents, each step visible in its thought-process view).
88: **Where a human must act:** at every HIL block, and when approving, rejecting, deferring or editing a
89: requirement, overriding a priority or answering a challenge on the Car tab. The AI can **never** set
90: a requirement to `approved` or `rejected`.
91: 
92: ## Core objects (full schemas in `packages/core`)
93: 
94: - **Source** — a dataset, document or web page, with a reliability rating.
95: - **SourceRecord** — one comment, row or paragraph from a source.
96: - **Finding** — a normalized signal (`complaint`, `unmet_need`, `praise`, `competitor_advantage`,
97:   `market_trend` or `usage_pattern`). It always cites ≥ 1 verbatim evidence excerpt.
98: - **Theme** — a cluster of duplicate or related findings.
99: - **Requirement** — `REQ-<vehicle>-<market>-<nnn>`. Holds the description, targets, linked findings and
100:   sources, score, priority with rationale, **evidence level A–D**, assumptions, uncertainties,
101:   conflicting findings and **status** (`proposed → in_review → approved | rejected | deferred`, plus
102:   `challenged`).
103: - **AuditEvent** — actor, action, entity, before/after changes, rationale and timestamp. Never edited or deleted.
104: 
105: ## Prioritization logic (explainable by design)
106: 
107: Six factors, each scored 0–5 with a one-line justification. On every factor, higher means "more worth doing":
108: customer impact · evidence strength · competitive gap · trend momentum (3–5 yr) · brand fit ·
109: ease (the inverse of rough effort/cost).
110: 
111: `score = 100 × Σ(weight × value) / (5 × Σ weight)`. The score maps to **must / should / could / won't**
112: using the thresholds set in Settings. The PM can override the priority, and the override is audited.
113: Evidence level is shown **next to** the score, never hidden inside it. A high score built on
114: D-level (assumption) evidence should catch the eye.
115: 
116: ## Evidence levels
117: 
118: **A** — several independent sources including quantitative BMW data · **B** — several sources, mostly
119: qualitative · **C** — a single source or anecdotal · **D** — rests mainly on forward-looking assumptions.
120: 
121: ## Scope rules (from the briefing)
122: 
123: - **In scope:** customer-facing attributes such as features, equipment, comfort, space, usability,
124:   infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging
125:   _as the customer experiences them_, and variants and packages.
126: - **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, technical and engineering specs, and
127:   pricing or business cases. An AI Filter removes these, and every exclusion is logged with a reason.
128: 
129: ## Demo scenario
130: 
131: **BMW 1 Series (F70) · EU · 5-year horizon**, because BMW's data is for the F70: customer feedback,
132: customer studies (the F70 next to the G60/G68 5 Series and G70 7 Series), sales volumes and the option
133: list. The requirements are for the F70's successor. This is the default scope in Settings.
134: 
135: 1. Open the default template, attach the BMW files to the Raw blocks, enable web research, and run.
136: 2. Watch the blocks fill up, then click the AI Filter to see findings with their evidence.
137: 3. The run pauses at the HIL block. On the Car tab, open a must-have and trace it down to a verbatim customer quote.
138: 4. Challenge one requirement. The AI answers. Edit one, approve one with a priority override, and reject one.
139: 5. Resume the run, which publishes and exports. The audit trail shows the full history of one requirement.
140: 6. Switch the scope to another series or market in Settings to show the workflow isn't a one-off.
141: 
142: ## Deliverables checklist (briefing → where we show it)
143: 
144: - [ ] Concept and working prototype → the app and this document
145: - [ ] Structured sample list of requirements with all the required fields → Car tab and export
146: - [ ] End-to-end workflow showing which steps the AI does alone and where a human must act → Data Flow tab (HIL blocks) and the diagram above
147: - [ ] Audit trail from source to decision → audit trail on the Car tab and the requirement History
148: 
149: ## Non-goals for the hackathon
150: 
151: Authentication, live multi-user editing and a sync server (Settings → Collaboration keeps the team and
152: the sharing choice on this computer; sending invitations and syncing come later, if at all), web and
153: mobile versions, signed installers and auto-update. Any of these can be mocked if the
154: demo needs them.

1: # Architecture
2: 
3: ReqFlow is a **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron), not a web app.
4: Background and alternatives: [decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md](decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md).
5: Why the flow is built from blocks: [decisions/0003-building-blocks.md](decisions/0003-building-blocks.md).
6: 
7: ## Stack
8: 
9: | Concern         | Choice                                                                                | Why                                                                 |
10: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
11: | Language        | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces)                                                | One shared contract for UI, engine and blocks                       |
12: | App shell       | Electron 44 (pinned, Node 24 inside), electron-vite 5, electron-builder               | Same Chromium on every OS; Node in the main process runs the engine |
13: | UI              | React 19 + React Router (hash routing) + Tailwind 4 + zustand 5                       | Renders from `file://` in the installed app; small, testable stores |
14: | Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow 12)                                                       | The standard n8n-style node editor                                  |
15: | Schemas         | Zod 4                                                                                 | Runtime validation and TS types from one source                     |
16: | LLM             | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider           | Swappable; works offline and in tests                               |
17: | Persistence     | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite`, in the OS app-data folder                          | Zero setup, no native module to rebuild per OS                      |
18: | Tests           | Vitest (colocated `*.test.ts`) + `npm run smoke` (clicks through the app in Electron) | Fast unit tests; a real-app check without clicking                  |
19: 
20: ## Repo layout
21: 
22: ```
23: .
24: ├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
25: ├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing + the app sketch (read-only)
26: ├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, STATUS, decisions/ (ADRs)
27: ├── data/
28: │   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
29: │   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
30: ├── packages/
31: │   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, blocks.ts (block specs), graph.ts (graph rules), IPC API, fixtures
32: │   ├── engine/     ← block contract + registry (done); executor (WS1)
33: │   ├── blocks/     ← block implementations, one folder per block + default template
34: │   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
35: │   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
36: └── apps/desktop/                      ← the Electron app
37:     ├── electron.vite.config.ts  electron-builder.yml  build/ (icons)
38:     └── src/
39:         ├── main/       ← Node: window, IPC handlers, wiring of engine/db/llm, smoke test
40:         ├── preload/    ← the bridge: allow-listed invoke + run-update events (keep tiny)
41:         └── renderer/src/
42:             ├── pages/        DataflowPage · CarPage · SettingsPage
43:             ├── components/   dataflow/ (editor + its store) · settings/ · shell/ (bottom tabs) · ui/ (shared controls)
44:             ├── lib/          api.ts (the only way to main) · settings.ts (settings store) · theme.ts
45:             └── router.tsx  globals.css (design tokens, light + dark)
46: ```
47: 
48: Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← blocks`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
49: `apps/desktop/src/main` → all of them. The renderer imports only `@reqflow/core` (types, block specs,
50: graph rules, fixtures). It never imports engine, db, llm or blocks.
51: 
52: ## Processes and security
53: 
54: ```
55: renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
56:    no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain
57:            ◀──────────────── runs.onUpdate(run) push events ────────────────────────┘
58: ```
59: 
60: - `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. Production builds get a strict CSP
61:   (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
62: - The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
63: - The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
64: - API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to
65:   the renderer. In dev, `apps/desktop/.env` is also read (see `.env.example`).
66: 
67: ## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)
68: 
69: A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
70: are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
71: it has an inner workplace):
72: 
73: | Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                                                   |
74: | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
75: | Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                                                            |
76: | Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel upload or database, dataset, file/query                                   |
77: | Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results                                    |
78: | AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence                                               |
79: | AI Splitter | 1 in · one out **per branch**         | no              | split by, branches (list → ports), model                                        |
80: | HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits                                        |
81: | Add to Car  | one in **per priority** + context ins | no              | priorities, contexts (Auto / Sales volumes), max. requirements, vehicle, market |
82: 
83: - **Ports** come from `blockPorts(block)`. They can depend on params (the splitter's `branches`, Add to
84:   Car's `priorities` → `in-0` "1. Priority" … and `contexts` → `ctx-0` "Context 1 · Auto" …), and port
85:   ids are positional (`out-0`, `in-2`, `ctx-0`). Older flows are migrated on load (`migrateGraph`). When params change, `setBlockParams`
86:   removes edges on ports that no longer exist and returns them, so the editor can tell the user.
87: - **Params** are declared as `ParamSpec`s (text, textarea, number, slider, select, multiselect, toggle,
88:   list — free text, or one of `itemOptions` per entry — and file). The editor renders a form from them, and `parseBlockParams` validates strictly (unknown
89:   keys and wrong types are errors). Select options with the value `"global"` mean "use Settings →
90:   Global parameters".
91: - **Inner workplaces** (Custom, Research, AI Filter) hold a sub-flow built from the same blocks,
92:   recursively. Each one has fixed **boundary blocks**: one `block_input` per input port of the parent
93:   and one `block_output` per output port. They are created with the block and can't be deleted.
94: - **Ids** are unique across the whole tree, so run status and outputs are keyed by block id alone.
95: - **Graph rules** live in `packages/core/src/graph.ts` and are shared by the editor and the engine:
96:   `checkConnection` (ports exist, no self-loop, no duplicates, no cycles), `connect`, `removeBlocks`,
97:   `setBlockParams`, `graphAt` / `updateGraphAt` (navigate the tree), `validateGraph` (everything,
98:   recursively). Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out).
99: 
100: ## Add to Car agents
101: 
102: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/agents/`. Code does everything that must be exact; models read,
103: group, write and judge. One run of the block:
104: 
105: ```
106: context reader ─┐ (sales volumes summarized by code; Auto: a data profile the reader explains)
107: analysts (map) ─┴→ synthesizer (themes) → code picks themes → architect ⇄ critic → judge → code
108: ```
109: 
110: - **Analysts** read the priority inputs in batches (≤ 50 records, ≤ 14k chars, one input per batch)
111:   and return signals with record refs and quotes. Code checks every quote against the record
112:   (`findVerbatim`; a quote that isn't verbatim becomes the record's opening words) and turns signals
113:   into `Finding`s. Upstream findings are reused as they are.
114: - **Synthesizer** groups signals into themes (per category when there are many, then a merge pass).
115:   **Code** picks the themes: most important input first, then evidence weight (mentions ÷ rank);
116:   single comments and themes below `maxRequirements` are listed as held back, never dropped silently.
117: - **Architect** writes one requirement per theme from its strongest signals and the context briefs;
118:   the **critic** reviews it (accept / one rewrite / reject) and scores the six factors.
119: - **Judge** answers four typed questions (backed by evidence? customer-facing? still wanted at launch?
120:   testable?) through a `DecisionClient`: TypeSafe Jev (a "System 1" decision model with calibrated
121:   probabilities) or any LLM answering the same questions.
122: - **Code** assigns ids, priority from the input rank (first third of n inputs must, then should,
123:   then could), the critic's weighted score, evidence level A–D, and the confidence: a weighted
124:   geometric mean of the judge's answers, evidence breadth, the critic's verdict and conflicts.
125: - Everything is recorded in a `ReasoningTrace` (`packages/core/src/reasoning.ts`), stored by run and
126:   block (`reasoning_traces`) and shown in the thought-process view (block button, inspector, Car → Why?).
127: - Each role runs on an API setup (Settings → AI → Agents; `apps/desktop/src/main/agents.ts`). Providers
128:   live in `packages/llm`: Claude (adaptive thinking by effort, summarized thinking kept for the trace),
129:   OpenAI / Gemini / OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, TypeSafe Jev, and the offline mock, which runs
130:   the same pipeline by rules and marks everything "[Offline]".
131: - `npm run eval:f70` runs the agents on BMW's F70 files with the user's setups and prints numbers only;
132:   the full output goes to `data/raw/eval/` (gitignored).
133: 
134: ## Data flow: one envelope per port
135: 
136: Every port carries a `PipelineData` envelope (`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`).
137: Raw and Research emit sources and records (the "unified data stream"). Later blocks enrich the same
138: envelope: AI Filter keeps matching items (and extracts evidence-linked findings), AI Splitter routes
139: items to one branch each, HIL passes on what the reviewer approved, and Add to Car's agents turn what
140: arrives on its priority inputs into requirements (the input it arrives on sets the ranking; context
141: inputs are background only, see "Add to Car agents"). Several edges into one input are combined
142: with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).
143: 
144: ```ts
145: defineBlock({
146:   kind: "ai_filter",
147:   async run(inputs, params, ctx) {
148:     const input = inputs.in; // one envelope per input port id
149:     /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */
150:     return { status: "ok", outputs: { out: kept } }; // one envelope per output port id
151:   },
152: });
153: ```
154: 
155: ## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)
156: 
157: 1. **Validate before running** with `validateGraph`, and check that every block kind (except
158:    Custom) has an implementation (`BlockRegistry.missing()`). If anything fails, the run fails before it
159:    starts, with per-block errors.
160: 2. **Execute each workplace in topological order.** A block's input per port is the merge of what its
161:    incoming edges carry. Store each block's output per port and push `BlockRun` status, counts, logs
162:    and progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
163: 3. **Inner workplaces.** A block whose inner workplace contains blocks runs that sub-flow: each
164:    `block_input` emits what arrived on its parent port, and what reaches each `block_output` becomes
165:    the parent's output on that port. A Custom block always runs its sub-flow. Research and AI Filter run
166:    their built-in implementation while their inner workplace is empty.
167: 4. **Failure.** A block that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream blocks `skipped`, and the run
168:    `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
169: 5. **Pause / resume.** HIL returns `{ status: "paused" }` → the run is `waiting_for_review`.
170:    `runs.resume` reloads what the reviewer changed, re-invokes the block with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
171: 6. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and blocks must stop promptly.
172: 7. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, blocks log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.
173: 
174: ## IPC API (`packages/core/src/ipc.ts`)
175: 
176: UI code calls `api.<namespace>.<method>(…)` from `@/lib/api`. Main implements `ReqflowHandlers`
177: (`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
178: (`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main
179: validates every argument with the Zod schemas, because the renderer counts as untrusted input.
180: 
181: | Method                                               | Purpose                                                                                                                                   |
182: | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
183: | `app.info()`                                         | Version, OS, data directory (**built**)                                                                                                   |
184: | `templates.list()`                                   | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) (**built**)                                                                                   |
185: | `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                     | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                                  |
186: | `blocks.preview(request)`                            | Runs a block without inputs (Raw) on its own and returns its output and log (**built**)                                                   |
187: | `files.import()`                                     | Native open dialog → copies the file into the data dir → `StoredFileInfo` (`null` if cancelled). Raw's `file` param stores it (**built**) |
188: | `runs.start/get/list/blockOutput/resume/cancel`      | Run lifecycle. `blockOutput` returns that block's output per port                                                                         |
189: | `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                            | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                          |
190: | `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)` | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                             |
191: | `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`             | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                                       |
192: | `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`       | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review`       |
193: | `requirements.reset()`                               | Removes every requirement (Car page → Reset). Writes one `requirement.deleted` audit event each; ids are never reused                     |
194: | `audit.list(filter)`                                 | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                           |
195: | `settings.get/save` · `settings.secrets/setSecret`   | `Settings` (save logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · API-key status / store a key in the keychain                                      |
196: | `exports.requirements({ runId, format })`            | Native save dialog → JSON / CSV / Markdown (logs `export.created`)                                                                        |
197: 
198: To add a method: add it to `ReqflowApi` **and** `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS` (the compiler enforces both),
199: then implement it in `handlers.ts`.
200: 
201: ## HIL review report
202: 
203: Double-clicking a HIL block (or its report icon) opens `components/dataflow/report/HilReport.tsx`:
204: 
205: - **Flow chart** from `traceLineage(root, path, blockId)` (`packages/core/src/lineage.ts`): every step
206:   data passes through on its way into the block. It leaves inner workplaces through their
207:   `block_input` and traces through the sub-flow of upstream blocks that have blocks inside.
208: - **Data at a step** (table icon on every step; the HIL itself = "data at this point"). Steps without
209:   inputs (Raw) show their **real data** via `blocks.preview`, and so does a HIL fed directly by them.
210:   After a run it shows `api.runs.blockOutput()` of the step (for the HIL: the merge of what its
211:   incoming edges carried). Otherwise it says nothing has arrived yet; there is no demo data.
212: - At run time the HIL block (`packages/blocks/src/hil/hil.ts`) pauses the run until the review is done
213:   and then passes the data on unchanged; edits go through the requirement API (audited).
214: 
215: ## Renderer state
216: 
217: - **`components/dataflow/store.ts`**: the editor store (zustand). It holds the workflow tree, the
218:   open workplace (`path`), the selection, React Flow sizes and a notice. Every edit goes through the
219:   core graph rules; errors become a visible notice, never a silent no-op. It lives for the whole app
220:   session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. It isn't saved to disk yet (`workflows.*` is WS1).
221: - **`lib/settings.ts`**: the settings store. It loads `settings.get()` at startup, validates every
222:   change with the `Settings` schema and saves in the background. While main has no settings storage
223:   (`not_implemented`), it keeps the defaults and the Settings page says so.
224: - **zustand 5 rule:** never return a new object or array from a selector (it re-renders forever).
225:   Select existing objects or primitives and derive the rest with `useMemo`.
226: - **Theme:** `lib/theme.ts` sets `<html data-theme>` from Settings (system, light or dark). The CSS
227:   tokens in `globals.css` follow it, so use token classes (`bg-panel`, `text-muted`, …), never hex colors.
228: - **Colorway: BMW M.** The M stripe colours (`m-light` #81C4FF, `m-dark` #16588E, `m-red` #E7222E) on
229:   carbon neutrals. Block groups take them: sources light blue, AI dark blue, HIL red (a person has to
230:   act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use
231:   `bg-brand-fill` so white text stays readable in both themes.
232: 
233: ## AI usage rules
234: 
235: - Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
236: - **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
237:   the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
238: - Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
239: - AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
240: - The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
241: - Prompts live next to the block that uses them (`blocks/src/<block>/<name>.prompt.ts`).
242: 
243: ## Persistence notes (WS1)
244: 
245: - The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
246:   `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
247:   `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
248:   with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
249: - Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
250: - Workflows are stored whole (the block tree as JSON) and versioned on save.
251: - Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
252: - `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
253: - Block outputs are stored per `(runId, blockId, port)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `uploads/`
254:   inside the data dir by the file store (`packages/db/src/files.ts`, built), metadata next to each file.
255: 
256: ## Running, checking, packaging
257: 
258: | Command (repo root) | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
259: | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
260: | `npm run dev`       | Opens the app with hot reload (renderer) and auto-restart (main)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
261: | `npm run smoke`     | Builds, then drives the real app off screen: opens every screen, adds every block, opens an inner workplace, types into fields, connects ports by mouse drag (and checks a loop is refused), walks the settings, switches to dark mode, screenshots each step to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any failed check or renderer error |
262: | `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
263: | `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
264: 
265: Installers must be built on their own OS (or in a CI matrix later). Builds are unsigned, so macOS
266: Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
267: hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.

1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.

85:     if (deg === 0) queue.push(id);
86:   }
87: 
88:   const sorted: WorkflowBlock[] = [];
89:   while (queue.length > 0) {
90:     const id = queue.shift()!;
91:     const block = blockMap.get(id);
92:     if (block) sorted.push(block);
93: 
94:     for (const edge of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
95:       if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
96:         const deg = inDegree.get(edge.target)! - 1;
97:         inDegree.set(edge.target, deg);
98:         if (deg === 0) queue.push(edge.target);
99:       }
100:     }
101:   }
102: 
103:   if (sorted.length < graph.blocks.length) {
104:     throw new EngineError("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
105:   }
106: 
107:   return sorted;
108: }

110: export function collectAllBlocks(graph: WorkflowGraph): WorkflowBlock[] {
111:   const blocks: WorkflowBlock[] = [];
112:   function recurse(g: WorkflowGraph) {
113:     for (const b of g.blocks) {
114:       blocks.push(b);
115:       if (b.inner) recurse(b.inner);
116:     }
117:   }
118:   recurse(graph);
119:   return blocks;

122: /** Splitters keep editable boundaries even when the built-in AI implementation runs. */

124:   return (
125:     !!block.inner &&
126:     block.inner.blocks.length > 0 &&
127:     (block.kind !== "ai_splitter" ||
128:       block.inner.edges.length > 0 ||
129:       block.inner.blocks.some((b) => !isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind)))

134:   return graph.blocks.flatMap((block) => [
135:     block,
136:     ...(usesInnerWorkplace(block) ? executableBlocks(block.inner!) : []),
137:   ]);

140: export function getDownstreamBlockIds(graph: WorkflowGraph, failedBlockId: string): Set<string> {
141:   const downstream = new Set<string>();
142:   const adj = new Map<string, string[]>();
143: 
144:   for (const b of graph.blocks) adj.set(b.id, []);
145:   for (const e of graph.edges) adj.get(e.source)?.push(e.target);
146: 
147:   const queue = [failedBlockId];
148:   while (queue.length > 0) {
149:     const curr = queue.shift()!;
150:     const neighbors = adj.get(curr) ?? [];
151:     for (const next of neighbors) {
152:       if (!downstream.has(next)) {
153:         downstream.add(next);
154:         queue.push(next);
155:       }
156:     }
157:   }
158: 
159:   return downstream;
160: }

4: export function jevClient(o: {
5:   baseUrl?: string;
6:   apiKey: string;
7:   model?: string;
8:   fetch?: typeof fetch;
9:   limiter?: Limiter;
10:   timeoutMs?: number;
11:   sleep?: (ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>;
12: }): DecisionClient {
13:   const limiter = o.limiter ?? new Limiter(4);
14:   const baseUrl = o.baseUrl || "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1";
15:   const model = o.model || "jev-latest";
16:   const timeoutMs = o.timeoutMs ?? 30000;
17: 
18:   return {
19:     async decide(request: DecisionRequest) {
20:       if (request.state.length > 100000) {
21:         throw new Error("The text is too long for Jev (max 100 000 characters)");
22:       }
23: 
24:       const url = baseUrl.endsWith("/") ? `${baseUrl}systemone` : `${baseUrl}/systemone`;
25: 
26:       const body = {
27:         state: request.state,
28:         model,
29:         questions: request.questions,
30:       };
31: 
32:       return limiter.run(async () => {
33:         const res = await postJson(url, {
34:           headers: {
35:             "content-type": "application/json",
36:             Authorization: `Bearer ${o.apiKey}`,
37:           },
38:           body,
39:           signal: request.signal,
40:           fetch: o.fetch ?? fetch,
41:           timeoutMs,
42:           provider: "TypeSafe",
43:           sleep: o.sleep,
44:         });
45: 
46:         const data = res.json as any;
47:         const answers: Record<string, any> = {};
48: 
49:         for (const [key, q] of Object.entries(request.questions)) {
50:           const ans = data.answers?.[key];
51:           if (!ans || ans.type !== q.type) {
52:             throw new Error(`Jev's answer to ${key} doesn't match the question`);
53:           }
54: 
55:           if (q.type === "noul") {
56:             if (typeof ans.noul !== "number" || ans.noul < 0 || ans.noul > 1) {
57:               throw new Error(`Jev's answer to ${key} doesn't match the question`);
58:             }
59:             answers[key] = { type: "noul", value: ans.noul };
60:           } else if (q.type === "score") {
61:             if (
62:               typeof ans.score !== "number" ||
63:               ans.score < 0 ||
64:               ans.score > q.criteria.length - 1
65:             ) {
66:               throw new Error(`Jev's answer to ${key} doesn't match the question`);
67:             }
68:             const probs: number[] = [];
69:             for (let i = 0; i < q.criteria.length; i++) {
70:               probs.push(ans.probabilities?.[i] ?? 0);
71:             }
72:             answers[key] = {
73:               type: "score",
74:               score: ans.score,
75:               probabilities: probs.map((p) =>
76:                 typeof p === "number" && Number.isFinite(p) ? p : 0,
77:               ),
78:               confidence: shapeConfidence(ans.confidence, probs),
79:             };
80:           } else if (q.type === "choice") {
81:             if (!q.criteria[ans.choice]) {
82:               throw new Error(`Jev's answer to ${key} doesn't match the question`);
83:             }
84:             const options = Object.keys(q.criteria);
85:             const probabilities = Object.fromEntries(
86:               options.map((opt) => {
87:                 const p = ans.probabilities?.[opt];
88:                 return [opt, typeof p === "number" && Number.isFinite(p) ? p : 0];
89:               }),
90:             );
91:             answers[key] = {
92:               type: "choice",
93:               choice: ans.choice,
94:               probabilities,
95:               confidence: shapeConfidence(ans.confidence, Object.values(probabilities)),
96:             };
97:           }
98:         }
99: 
100:         const usage = {
101:           inputTokens: data.usage?.input_tokens ?? 0,
102:           outputTokens: data.usage?.output_tokens ?? 0,
103:         };
104: 
105:         return {
106:           answers,
107:           model: data.model ?? model,
108:           usage,
109:         };
110:       }, request.signal);
111:     },
112:   };

**Recommendation**
Make the AI Filter a **selection-only block**, not a rewriting or extraction block:

> AI decides which item IDs match the user’s criteria. Code passes through the original items unchanged. A separate report records every decision and its reason.

For the demo, I would start with structured LLM classification. Add vector comparison or Jev only if evaluation shows a clear benefit.

**Current Gaps**
The code explains why the filter is not functional yet:

- There is no registered implementation: `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/index.ts:4` exports an empty list.
- The inspector already defines `criterion`, `model`, `minConfidence` and `keepUnsure`: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts:337`.
- There is also an execution issue: new filters contain boundary blocks, but the engine treats any non-empty filter workplace as a custom sub-flow. The boundary-only exception currently applies only to the Splitter: `packages/engine/src/executor.ts:123`. Registering a filter implementation alone would therefore not fix newly created filters.
- The product documentation currently combines filtering with finding extraction. That conflicts with your requested “output the remaining data without altering it.” I recommend separating these responsibilities.

These are code-inspection findings; I have not run or changed the app.

**Options**

| Approach | How It Works | Advantages | Limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Explicit rules** | Filter by metadata, configured fields, dates, markets or clear exclusion rules. | Fast, predictable, easy to explain, runs locally. | Cannot reliably understand nuanced relevance. Keywords can remove useful information accidentally. |
| **2. Structured LLM classifier** | Give the model criteria and items; require `keep`, `exclude` or `review`, with a reason and supporting quote for each ID. | Flexible prompts; understands context, mixed topics and multilingual feedback. Simplest useful AI implementation. | Cost and latency; decisions can vary. Model-reported confidence is not automatically calibrated. |
| **3. Vector comparison** | Embed each item and compare it with user-approved relevant and irrelevant examples. | Efficient for large datasets; shows similar examples; embeddings can be cached. | Similarity is not relevance. Negation, numbers and mixed-topic comments are difficult. Similarity scores are not probabilities. |
| **4. Jev decision model** | Ask typed questions such as “Does this item contain information relevant to the stated scope?” and apply a documented decision policy. | Fits the existing `DecisionClient` integration; gives structured decision scores. | The current Jev adapter returns decisions and scores, not textual explanations. A separate explanatory step is needed. Live integration is still unverified according to the handoff. |
| **5. Hybrid pipeline** | Use explicit rules for unambiguous cases, vectors for comparison, and an LLM or Jev for ambiguous cases. | Potentially balances scale, cost and quality; disagreements become review cases. | More components and thresholds to evaluate. Harder to build and explain during a hackathon. |

For vectors, the report should say **“similar to these excluded examples”**, not invent a semantic explanation from a cosine score. For Jev, any explanation generated by another model must be labelled as such, rather than presented as Jev’s actual reasoning.

**Suggested Design**
Start with Option 2, supported by a few explicit metadata rules.

1. **Define relevance.** The user chooses a preset or writes inclusion/exclusion criteria, with optional examples.
2. **Classify bounded batches.** The model returns decisions and annotations only, never replacement data.
3. **Validate the response.** Every input ID must receive exactly one decision. Reject unknown IDs, duplicates, missing decisions and non-verbatim supporting quotes.
4. **Select original objects.** Build the output from the input objects using the accepted IDs, preserving content, fields, metadata, IDs and order.
5. **Save a separate decision report.** Store the original input snapshot, decisions, effective criteria, model/version and human overrides locally.

Uncertainty should default to **keep and flag for review**, not exclude. Provider errors or malformed answers should visibly fail the step, never produce an apparently successful empty output.

A critical rule is:

> **Relevant does not mean positive, popular or consistent with existing evidence.**

Praise, complaints, minority needs and contradictory evidence can all be relevant. The filter must not hide inconvenient evidence.

**Customization**
I would expose these parameters:

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Relevance instruction** | Plain-language definition of what should pass through. |
| **Include / exclude criteria** | Explicit boundaries, such as customer-facing usability versus dealer administration. |
| **Examples** | User-labelled examples of relevant and irrelevant items. |
| **Context** | Vehicle, market and horizon, with optional overrides from Settings. |
| **Fields to assess** | Which text or table columns inform classification; other fields remain untouched. |
| **Uncertainty policy** | Keep and flag, or require a downstream HIL review. |
| **Exclusion threshold** | How strong the evidence must be before excluding an item. |
| **Model / method** | LLM initially; Jev or hybrid later. |

Customization should affect relevance policy, but must not override the fixed guarantees about unchanged output, complete decision coverage and auditability.

**Review Experience**
Clicking the filter should show **Kept · Excluded · Needs Review**, with a searchable table containing:

- Original item and source location.
- Decision and matched criterion.
- Short explanation with a verified supporting quote.
- Model score, labelled accurately.
- Whether it passed downstream.
- Human override and rationale.

Excluded data is **excluded from this output, not deleted from the project**. A PM can restore it, with an audit event. If downstream execution has already occurred, restoring an item must trigger an explicit rerun rather than silently changing previous results.

The current audit schema has `finding.excluded`, but no record-level filtering action (`packages/core/src/audit.ts:23`). We should propose a proper filter-decision contract rather than mislabel raw records as findings.

**Preservation Boundary**
If one comment contains both relevant and irrelevant information, strict preservation means **keeping the whole comment** whenever the relevant portion qualifies.

For example, a synthetic comment mentioning both dealer administration and uncomfortable seats should remain unchanged because seat comfort is relevant. Removing only the dealer sentence would be extraction or editing, not selection-only filtering.

Similarly, filtering findings or requirements must preserve their linked evidence, including conflicting evidence. Supporting records may remain because a retained item references them; the report should explain that.

**What I Would Choose**
For this project:

1. Implement structured LLM classification with unchanged pass-through and a complete decision report.
2. Evaluate against human-labelled synthetic cases, prioritizing **how much relevant information gets wrongly excluded**.
3. Compare Jev and vector-assisted classification on the same cases before introducing them into the pipeline.

The main product choice to confirm is: **should a mixed-topic item always remain intact when any part is relevant?** I recommend yes, to satisfy your preservation requirement.
implement your suggested plan
I’ll map the implementation against the existing engine, audit storage and report UI. Plan mode is active, so I’ll prepare the concrete changes and verification steps without modifying files.

## Required new contracts

### Structured model response
Use an explicit protocol such as `reqflow.ai-filter.selection@1`:

```ts
{
  decisions: [{
    id,
    decision: "keep" | "exclude" | "review",
    confidence: number, // 0–1
    reason: string     // bounded, nonblank explanation
  }]
}

- `schemaVersion`, `runId`, `blockId`, `createdAt`.
- Primary layer and input counts.
- Criterion and applied `minConfidence` / `keepUnsure` policy.
- Per item: ID, model decision, effective decision, confidence, reason, actual model ID, and whether emitted.
- Aggregate keep/exclude/review and output counts.
- Missing-reference/closure warnings and an explicit offline marker.

### Policy to settle before coding
Recommended:
- Explicit model `review` remains `review`.
- `keep` or `exclude` below `minConfidence` becomes effective `review`.
- Emit effective `keep`; emit effective `review` only when `keepUnsure`.
- Confidence equal to the threshold passes.
- `review` is metadata, **not a paused run**: the engine permits only HIL to pause.

Reuse primary-layer precedence `requirements → themes → findings → records` unless the product explicitly wants record-first filtering. Specify empty and source-only behavior; a reasonable default is no model call, with source-only input preserved as unclassified context and reported accordingly.

1. **Splitter’s orphan retention would defeat filtering.**  
   Do not call `retainOrphans` unchanged: excluded items would look unreferenced and be reintroduced.

2. **Closure can reintroduce excluded primary items.**  
   Existing closure traverses finding → theme → sibling findings. Keeping one finding can therefore retain another classified `exclude`. Decide whether such items may remain as **evidence-only context**, or whether closure should omit optional theme enrichment. Report this distinction explicitly; silently filtering closure afterward can leave dangling links. Full closure, unchanged references, and absolute removal of every excluded primary item can conflict.

3. **The raw Splitter selector is not complete evidence closure.**

4. **Preserve originals, not parsed copies.**  
   Entity schemas strip unknown fields. Validate then select from the original input; preserve provenance, fields, text, IDs, requirement status and scoring. The engine clones outputs, so cross-process reference identity is not promised.

5. **Partial envelopes are currently allowed.**  
   Missing dependencies should remain missing, with warnings—not fabricated evidence or rewritten IDs. Existing validation checks source consistency and verbatim excerpts when the referenced record is available.

6. **Local persistence does not imply local inference.**  
   Real providers receive item content and evidence. Keep prompts bounded, treat all source content as untrusted data, and never print prompts, excerpts or model reasons into run logs.

7. **Persistence is ordered, not atomic.**

A crash can leave stored output without the matching succeeded report. If atomic report/output durability is required, add a transactional repository operation and wire it through the executor and desktop handler; inline JSON alone does not supply that guarantee.

8. **Inner workplaces can bypass the built-in Filter.**  
   Boundary-only workplaces use the implementation; authored inner edges/blocks execute the subflow instead. Preserve this existing behavior and test it.

9. **Mock must be honest.**  
   The current mock recognizes only explicit Splitter protocols. Add Filter support deliberately; unsupported semantic criteria should produce review or a clear error, not arbitrary hash-based exclusions presented as AI judgment.

- Every primary layer; mixed envelopes; empty/source-only input; wrong input ports and duplicate IDs.
- Frozen input: original values, extension fields, order and statuses unchanged.
- Supporting **and conflicting** evidence closure; shared evidence; theme cycles/siblings; missing references.
- Excluded items not resurrected by orphan retention; explicit handling of excluded-as-context dependencies.
- All-excluded output still has `out`, valid empty arrays and preserved envelope metadata.
- Batch count/size boundaries; oversized individual item fails without truncation.
- Cancellation before/during/after generation, including a transport ignoring `AbortSignal`; no accepted partial output/report.
- Prompt-injection fixtures; logs/errors contain neither source text nor model reasons.
- Mock determinism and truthful offline labeling; offline provider-schema/Mastra tests.
- Engine report kind/run/block mismatch rejection.
- SQLite round-trip and restart retrieval, including excluded decisions; older runs without reports remain valid.
- Persistence failure/crash-window behavior and authored versus placeholder inner workplaces.

**Implementation Plan**
The cross-path changes are authorized. Plan mode still prevents edits, so implementation will begin once it is disabled.

1. **Implement selection-only filtering.** Classify each primary item as `keep`, `exclude` or `needs_review`. Return original objects unchanged and in their original order. Mixed-topic items remain intact when any part is relevant. No finding extraction, rewriting or requirement-status changes.

2. **Add configurable criteria.** Extend the existing inspector with editable presets, inclusion/exclusion instructions, labelled examples and fields to assess. Reuse existing AI configuration and model controls. Low-confidence decisions become review cases; uncertain items pass through by default.

3. **Validate every AI response.** Require exactly one decision per input ID, a bounded explanation and verified supporting quotes where applicable. Unknown IDs, missing decisions, invalid quotes and malformed responses fail visibly. Batch requests without silently truncating input; support cancellation and an explicitly labelled offline mock.

4. **Preserve evidence dependencies.** Retain the available supporting and conflicting evidence referenced by selected items. Report any otherwise excluded item retained as supporting context, rather than silently reintroducing it. Preserve all original fields and provenance.

5. **Persist a selection report.** Store decisions separately from the data, with the effective criteria, model identity, scores and input provenance. Keep excluded originals reviewable locally after restart. Add appropriate record-level filter audit actions rather than misusing `finding.excluded`.

6. **Add review and restoration.** Reuse the existing report shell for searchable **Kept / Excluded / Needs Review** views. Show originals, source locations, reasons and forwarding status. “Restore on next run” requires a human rationale and writes an audit event. It never changes historical outputs or automatically resumes/reruns the workflow; changed content or criteria invalidate stale overrides.

7. **Verify end to end.** Add synthetic tests for unchanged output, complete classification coverage, threshold boundaries, mixed topics, conflicting evidence, cancellation, persistence and overrides. Run `npm run check` and `npm run smoke`, then inspect native Electron screenshots in light, dark and minimum-window layouts.

**Scope**
Use a separate branch/worktree so the current `ws5-pdf-ingestion` checkout remains untouched. Update the product definition to distinguish filtering from extraction, and record only this assigned feature in the handoff.

Vectors and Jev remain outside this first implementation. No confidential BMW data or live provider calls will be used without permission.
