# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI

8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't
   remove its hooks (`.claude/settings.json`, `.git/hooks`) and never put secrets in prompts.

9. **Hand off in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).** Claim your workstream there when you start; your
   tasks are the checklist in its section, in priority order. Update your own section (and only that
   one) when you finish a slice, get blocked or stop: tick done tasks, add a log entry. The next agent
   starts from it. The repo and Entire transcripts are **public**, so never paste keys or BMW data anywhere.

### Findings

1. **P1 — Offline mock excludes relevant mixed-topic evidence with high confidence.**  
   **File:** `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/packages/llm/src/mock.ts:523–549`  
   Any out-of-scope keyword causes `exclude` at confidence `0.8` when the limited customer vocabulary does not match. For example, **“Acceleration is excellent, but the price is high”** is excluded despite containing relevant driving-experience praise. With blank `fields` (“all”), the mock also ignores `item.fields` and evidence context: a record with `text: "Pricing is high"` and `fields: { feature: "seat comfort" }` is excluded. Both bypass the default uncertainty protection because `0.8` exceeds the `0.7` threshold.  
   **Fix:** Assess structured fields/context when configured to assess all, and default to review unless irrelevance can actually be established. Add regression cases for mixed topics outside the keyword vocabulary and relevance present only in structured fields.

2. **P2 — Structured records with empty text cannot satisfy quote validation.**  
   **File:** `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/ai-filter.ts:214–228`  
   A schema-valid record with `text: ""`, `fields: { rating: 5 }`, and selected field `rating` makes `assessedText` truthy. The classifier then requires a quote from that record, but quote validation requires a nonblank substring of its empty `text`. No possible response can pass—even a conservative `review` response—so the whole filter fails on otherwise valid structured input.  
   **Fix:** Require text quotes only when the record has quotable nonblank text. Preserve structured-only evidence without manufacturing quotes.

3. **P2 — Classification audits can persist a partial, uncommitted selection.**  
   **File:** `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/ai-filter.ts:316–341`  
   Classification events are persisted individually before the report/output is returned. If the second audit write fails, the first remains committed, including its final outcome and `forwarded: true`, while the block fails and publishes neither report nor output. Cancellation between writes produces the same partial audit state. These events record a selection change without indicating that its forwarding was never committed. Human restoration writes are transactional; classification writes are not.  
   **Fix:** Commit classification events with accepted report/output through an atomic persistence operation, or explicitly distinguish attempted classifications from committed selections and record their failed/aborted disposition.

4. **P2 — Opening the report during execution leaves restoration state unavailable after completion.**  
   **File:** `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/report/FilterPanel.tsx:142–165`  
   A filter report becomes available while downstream blocks are still running. Opening it then calls `filterReviewState`, which rejects running runs (`/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter/apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts:442–447`). The effect depends only on run ID and block ID, so transitioning to `completed` or `waiting_for_review` never retries the request. `pending` remains null and restoration stays disabled until the user manually refreshes or reopens the panel.  
   **Fix:** Load state when the run enters an eligible stopped status, retaining the existing epoch guard for stale responses.

327:       run: session.run,
328:       registry: this.options.registry,

352:               : update.status === "cancelled"
353:                 ? "run.cancelled"
354:                 : "run.failed",

363:   private async fail(session: RunSession, error: unknown): Promise<never> {
364:     // Infrastructure failures must be observable, not mistaken for successful blocks or swallowed.
365:     const run = structuredClone(session.run);
366:     run.status = session.controller.signal.aborted ? "cancelled" : "failed";
367:     run.error = message(error);
368:     run.finishedAt = now();
369:     for (const state of run.blockRuns) {
370:       if (state.status === "succeeded" && session.savedOutputs[state.blockId]) continue;
371:       if (state.status === "failed" || state.status === "skipped") continue;
372:       state.status = state.status === "running" ? "failed" : "skipped";
373:       state.finishedAt = run.finishedAt;
374:       if (state.status === "failed") state.error = run.error;
375:     }
376:     session.run = run;
377:     try {
378:       await this.recordAudit(run.status === "cancelled" ? "run.cancelled" : "run.failed", run);
379:     } catch {
380:       // The original infrastructure error remains the operation's rejection.
381:     }
382:     // A failed persistence channel may fail again. Retain the failure in memory and reject the operation.
383:     try {
384:       await this.options.onUpdate?.(structuredClone(run));
385:     } catch {
386:       /* Original error is rethrown below. */
387:     }
388:     throw error;
389:   }

397:     void operation.catch(() => {});

Implemented and merged into `main`: [PR #22](https://github.com/EHL-Team-Eichel/reqflow/pull/22).

The AI Filter now:
- Selects relevant items **without rewriting their content, fields, IDs or order**, preserving linked evidence.
- Supports customizable criteria, inclusion/exclusion instructions, examples and field selection.
- Shows **Kept / Excluded / Needs Review** with original data, explanations, verified quotes and model information.
- Keeps uncertain items by default and supports audited human restoration **on an explicit later run**, without changing historical outputs or automatically continuing the flow.

**Verification**
- Full check passed: **2,474 tests passed, 6 skipped**.
- Native Electron smoke passed: **80 screenshots**, including inspected light, dark and minimum-window Filter views.
- Merged `main` matches the verified code.

Live-provider relevance quality remains untested. The offline mock is explicitly labelled; vector and Jev filtering were not included.

The verified checkout is at `../EHL-ai-filter`. Your original checkout and concurrent changes were left untouched.

## Goal

Implement ReqFlow’s previously nonfunctional **AI Filter** so it removes irrelevant input items while passing retained data through **unchanged**. Provide customizable relevance instructions and transparent, source-linked explanations of what was filtered and why.

The assigned feature is **complete and merged into `main`**. No further work is authorized.

## Instructions

- ReqFlow is a native Electron desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, not a web app.
- Work only on explicit human assignments; repository task lists and suggested next steps do not authorize follow-on work.
- The user initially requested options, then explicitly requested implementation of the recommended selection-only LLM approach.
- The user explicitly authorized necessary coordinated changes across core contracts, engine, database, main process and renderer.
- Preserve retained items’ original text, fields, IDs, provenance and order. Keep mixed-topic items intact if any part is relevant.
- Keep uncertain items by default. Praise, complaints, minority needs and contradictory evidence must not be discarded merely for their stance.
- Human restoration must require a rationale, be audited, and apply only on an **explicit later full run**. Never mutate historical output, automatically start/resume flows, or change requirement approval statuses.
- No secrets or confidential BMW data in public prompts, transcripts, code or logs. Implementation and verification used synthetic data; no live-provider or confidential-data evaluation was performed.
- Commit and push working slices; merge with merge commits, preserving Entire checkpoints. Verify with `npm run check` and native smoke screenshots.
- Stop after completing this assignment; any live-model evaluation or additional vectors/Jev work needs a new human assignment.

## Discoveries

- Initial inspection found `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/index.ts` exported an empty implementation array.
- An older engine had a boundary-only inner-workplace bypass bug. The newer implementation baseline already fixed it through `usesInnerWorkplace` in `research-kernel.ts`; no redundant fix was needed.
- Existing Splitter report/UI patterns were reusable for Filter report transport and inspection.
- The original documentation combined filtering with finding extraction. This assignment intentionally separates them: Filter performs **selection only**, with extraction downstream.
- The Filter classifies the most advanced populated layer: requirements → themes → findings → records. Source-only inputs pass through as explicitly unclassified context.
- Evidence closure can retain otherwise excluded primary items when needed by selected items. These are explicitly marked **retained as supporting context**, rather than silently reintroduced.
- Raw imports refresh `Source.retrievedAt` on every run. Including this timestamp in restoration fingerprints initially invalidated unchanged-data restorations; it is now excluded from dependency fingerprinting. Actual evidence/configuration/model changes still invalidate overrides.
- Structured-only records with empty text must not require impossible text quotes; this was corrected.
- The offline mock is intentionally narrow and labelled. It supports the customer-facing preset, conservatively reviews unfamiliar/custom semantic criteria, and avoids excluding mixed-topic content solely on pricing/regulation keywords.
- Classification audit writes are individually persisted **attempts, not publication events**. Their payload explicitly says `publication: "not_committed"` and does not claim forwarding. A succeeded saved report/output establishes actual publication.
- Default Vitest concurrency caused resource-contention timeouts when run alongside smoke. The complete gate passed using `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4 npm run check`, with smoke run sequentially.
- Agent CLIs were available and delegation was attempted. Headless `agy-delegate` editing was denied; scoped agents implemented with `apply_patch`, and the main agent reviewed and reran verification.

## Accomplished

### Completed implementation
- Registered strict, batched AI classification using protocol `reqflow.ai-filter.selection@1`.
- Required exact, unique ID coverage and validated decisions, confidence, reasons and verbatim quotes.
- Preserved original objects and evidence dependencies; added cancellation and visible failure handling without accepting partial filtered output.
- Added configurable criterion, include/exclude instructions, labelled examples, selected fields, model tier, confidence threshold and uncertainty forwarding policy.
- Added explicit presets and visible warnings when an authored inner workplace bypasses built-in filtering.
- Persisted full original input and per-item keep/exclude/review decisions in `BlockRun.filterReport`.
- Added searchable, paginated Filter reports with originals, quotes, source locations, configuration/model metadata, dispositions and uncertainty caveats.
- Added append-only SQLite human restorations with optimistic version checks and atomic restoration/audit writes.
- Added IPC `runs.filterReviewState` and `runs.reviewFilter`.
- Restorations bind to workflow/block, original item/evidence content, effective configuration, scope and model. Historical reports/outputs remain unchanged; application requires an explicit new run.
- Updated product/architecture documentation and the assigned handoff section.
- Added extensive synthetic unit/integration tests and native smoke scenarios.

### Integration and repository state
- Original checkout: `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL`, on `ws5-pdf-ingestion`; concurrent changes were left untouched.
- Feature worktree: `/Users/johannesnirschl/Documents/temporary/EHL-ai-filter`.

- `docs/STATUS.md` marks the human-assigned Filter feature done and agent released; other WS7 tasks remain unclaimed.

content.text:
**WS8 is the only workstream that is still essentially unbuilt.** WS2, WS3, WS4, WS5, WS7 and WS9 have remaining tasks, but already have substantial working functionality. WS1 and WS6 are implemented, with verification limits.

I checked the latest remote state and [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md). Some checkboxes are outdated: later entries confirm that features such as AI Filter, Car details, HIL PDF export and saved model settings have already been integrated.

## What Each Workstream Does

| WS | In simple words, when fully implemented | What still needs doing |
|---|---|---|
| **WS0: Integration** | Makes all the pieces work together and prepares a reliable demonstration. | Complete the full demo flow with a real AI model and actual datasets, rehearse the demo, update outdated status entries, and get a clean full-app smoke test on the latest combined version. |
| **WS1: Engine & Storage** | The app’s machinery: runs workflows, saves data, pauses for human review, and records changes. | **Original checklist complete.** Follow-up gaps are documented around multiple reviewers, recorded reviewer identity/rationale, and recovering paused execution after restarting the app. |
| **WS2: Flow Editor** | Lets you build and manage your analysis process by connecting blocks, then watch it run. | Undo/redo; copy/paste/duplicate; a proper save/load/autosave interface; clearer problem highlighting; richer block-by-block status/output inspection; automatic layout and editor polish. Starting, cancelling, templates and human-review continuation already work. |
| **WS3: Car Review** | Shows proposed improvements on the car, explains their evidence, and lets the product manager make decisions. | Approve/reject/defer/challenge controls; editing with reasons; a usable audit/history timeline; requirement export controls; filters and sorting; correcting automatic car-part placement. The 3D car, compact cards, detailed evidence and originating-workflow reports already work. |
| **WS4: Settings & Packaging** | Lets users configure the app and AI providers, then install it like a normal desktop application. | App icons, installer verification across Windows/macOS/Linux, installation instructions and final interface polish. Automated cross-platform checks are optional. Saved settings, secure credentials and model/powertrain selection already work; macOS packaging has been exercised in individual feature checks. |
| **WS5: Data Import** | Turns spreadsheets, PDFs and database results into usable data without losing the original evidence. | Automatically derive comparisons from customer-study figures; test performance with very large files; add column mapping if necessary. PostgreSQL/SQL Server support is conditional on need. XLSX/CSV/SQLite and PDF extraction are implemented; successful live PDF-AI validation remains blocked by the unavailable Gemini key. |
| **WS6: Research** | Collects outside information, such as reviews, competitors and trends, and keeps the original sources attached. | **Implementation checklist complete.** Real API/account testing, Windows/Linux verification and optional document-conversion tooling remain. Offline and macOS checks do not establish that every external service works live. |
| **WS7: AI Blocks** | Filters irrelevant data, sorts relevant items, and turns evidence into proposed car requirements with explanations. | Connect WS8’s scoring to the Splitter; implement “challenge this requirement” answers; evaluate and tune with real AI; test TypeSafe Jev live; complete the specifically listed Filter → Splitter → Add to Car offline regression. Filter, Splitter and Add to Car are implemented and merged. |
| **WS8: Prioritization** | Explains **which improvements matter most and why**, instead of relying on an opaque AI ranking. | **Entire workstream remains open:** calculate customer impact, evidence strength, competitive gap and trends; assess brand fit/effort; produce understandable reasons and weak-evidence warnings; verify that changing weights changes rankings; connect it to the Splitter. |
| **WS9: Analytics** | Shows charts comparing datasets, topics, countries and changes over time, without using AI to invent conclusions. | Save calculated analytics with each run instead of recalculating them; validate against the actual export formats and tune topic detection. Charts and comparison functionality are implemented and integrated, but the latest full-app smoke verification is incomplete. |

## Most Important Gaps

For the core product, rather than additional visual polish, I would prioritize:

1. **WS3: Human decision controls.** The product manager should be able to review, decide and edit directly in the interface.
2. **WS8 + WS7: Explainable prioritization.** Make the ranking defensible and connect it to the existing flow.
3. **WS2: Workflow management.** Make saving, reopening and changing workflows convenient and reliable.
4. **WS0 + WS6 + WS7: Real-model verification.** Prove the complete process works beyond the offline mock.
5. **WS4: Distribution.** Verify that the desktop app installs and runs on the intended platforms.

**Bottom line:** most of the pipeline exists. The biggest unfinished pieces are **transparent scoring, the PM’s decision interface, editor usability, and real-world end-to-end verification**.
